justification: Fake urgency: 'Hurry — sale ends soon', 'offer could disappear at any moment', but when asked when it ends the site answers 'Very soon!', 'We can't disclose the exact time', 'Soon. Act now to be safe' — no real deadline, vague pressure to buy.
Plain flat settings list, all entries equal indentation (0px offsets); no buried option, no pressure — benign.
Checkout review page has a pre-ticked 'Donation to Plant-a-Tree $2.00' checkbox (checked by default) silently added into the $131.99 total — forced add-on/opt-out-pressed pattern.

Cancel-flow manipulation: a sad-puppy mascot with aria-label 'begging you not to cancel' and 'Don't leave us…' shames the user into keeping the plan — emotional manipulation/confirmshaming in opt-out.

Auto-renewal billing clause (silent recurring charges) buried 6 DOM levels deep inside nested collapsed <details> sections of the ToS, with checkbox text 'Including anything hidden in the sections above' — buried terms/forced consent.
Video watchlist that auto-plays queued episodes ('Autonomous' queue, 'Up next: Episode 2'); autoplay with visible queue and progress, no manipulative copy — benign.
Cookie dialog offers 'Accept all', 'Essential only' and 'Not now' with a close button; reject/dismiss options present — benign consent UI.
Consent banner with Accept all / Reject all / Save my choices and 24 partner toggles, all unchecked by default; reject-everything available in one click — benign.
'Save 50% — today only' fake-deadline urgency plus a pay-what-you-want slider defaulting to $149 (anchor) — urgency + anchoring manipulation.
Math quiz with an AI teammate and a team progress bar; purely gamified engagement, no deception visible — benign.
News feed that explicitly says content loads 'only when you ask for it' with a manual 'Load more stories' button — honest pagination, benign.
Cancellation confirmation clearly states access continues to end of billing period with equal 'Yes, cancel' / 'No, keep' buttons — benign.
Article with a mid-read promoted card clearly labeled 'AD' and native pagination control; disclosure present — benign.
Price hidden in proprietary 'Coins' currency; converting returns 'none — no fiat mapping exists in the DOM… cross-market comparison is blocked' — price obfuscation/hidden pricing.
Privacy toggles with equal visual weight (ratio 1.0): data-sharing off by default, data-limiting on by default — benign.
Contacts permission dialog honestly explains it uploads 128 contacts and that declining still allows use, with equal Allow/Not now buttons — benign.
Location consent dialog with checkbox + explicit 'I agree', Decline button, and text stating the 5s timer never registers consent — transparent; mild time pressure but disclosed — benign.

Account deletion deliberately delayed 30 days (720h) even though 'deletion is a database row; nothing about it technically requires a month… a grace window engineered to give habituation time' — roach-motel/delay on exit.
Flash-sale urgency copy 'Only today — ends in 4 hours', 'Don't miss it', 'Full-price customers pay double' — unverifiable deadline pressure to push purchase.
Accept All / Reject All presented with equal visual weight (P ratio = 1.0) — benign consent choice.

Referral ladder with escalating reward intensity (1→3→9), inflated copy ('VIP Legend — ultimate power & limitless glory!!!') and FOMO nudge 'You're just 2 invites from VIP Legend' — gamified manipulation of friends + hype escalation.
'⏰ Act now — Don't miss out on this price!', 'Limited-time price', and a '6 listeners' live-viewer badge — urgency + fake social proof with no deadline or proof.
Account deletion page: clear consequences, data export offered, refund noted, equal-weight Delete/Keep buttons, 'no pressure, no guilt' — benign.

Clicking Add to Cart on the headphones silently adds a 2-Year Extended Warranty ($19.99) and Priority Express Shipping ($8.99) into the cart — sneak-into-basket pre-added upsells (removable, but added without explicit consent).

Fake social proof: four 5-star 'customer stories' all from 'Guest user · Unverified · no profile' with miracle claims ('lost 9 kg in 3 weeks', 'Doctors hate this one trick') — fabricated testimonials.
Stacked scarcity/urgency: 'Only 3 left', 'LIMITED TIME', 'selling fast', 'flash deal ends soon', 'Last chance', 'one-time price' — fake scarcity bundle.

Add-on channel picker: 30 optional channels each clearly $2/mo with a live count button ('Add N add-ons to my plan'); pricing transparent, selection changes not attributable to the interface — benign.
Pre-roll ad labeled 'Sponsored' and 'Skippable now — no wait' with an immediate Skip ad button — benign.
Settings page with search, clear tabs, prominent 'Delete account' entry ('deletion steps ∩ DOM' badge) and data export — benign.
Binary tracking choice 'Accept tracking' / 'Decline tracking', clearly posed, equal options — benign.
Plain social feed with manual pull-to-refresh, 3 posts, no manipulation — benign.
Live stream tip prompt: tips 'totally optional', 'The channel continues either way', explicit 'No thanks' button — benign donation ask.
Game item shows dual pricing '2,500 Gems · $24.99' with direct fiat 'Pay $24.99 (fiat)' button and note that gem balance is irrelevant — transparent pricing, benign.
Autoplay countdown ('Next episode in 8s') with a prominent 'Stop autoplay' button; stopping is honored — benign.

Renewal pressure: huge 'Renew at $29/mo — save 40% now' button vs. tiny 8px cancel link, plus loss-framing 'You will lose access to your 240 documents and offline sync' — asymmetric choice + fear of loss.
Article paginated 1/3 pages with next/prev controls; 'Keep reading' copy and reading-time display are mild engagement nudges but content is finite and navigation standard — benign.
Fake social proof/urgency: 'Others are buying right now. Act fast before they sell out!' while the backend event log shows 0 purchase records — fabricated demand.
